description: We are a team of creative students interested in technology, space, and sustainable agriculture. Our project, VIRDARA, explores how satellite data and AI can support smarter farming decisions. Our interests include web development, UI/UX, Python, data research, and prototyping. We welcome curious and motivated teammates, especially those with skills in agriculture, GIS, remote sensing, data analysis, AI, and web development. Let's build something meaningful together!
summary:
VIRDARA is an agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make more informed and resilient farming decisions in the face of changing environmental conditions. It brings together soil assessment, climate information, crop rotation planning, and farm economic analysis in one integrated interface.

By combining user-provided farm information with environmental data from sources such as NASA POWER and weather services, VIRDARA helps users explore agricultural conditions, compare crop rotation strategies, and understand potential risks and economic outcomes. Its tools connect environmental insights with practical planning, making complex information easier to interpret and use.

VIRDARA addresses the need for more accessible, data-informed agricultural decision-making. By bringing different factors into one platform, it aims to support more thoughtful resource management, improve planning, and contribute to more resilient agricultural systems.
details:
Project Details

VIRDARA is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that connects environmental information, soil assessment, crop rotation planning, and farm economics to help users make more informed agricultural decisions.

How It Works

VIRDARA brings several important aspects of farm planning into one interface:

  • Soil Assessment: Users can enter available soil properties and previous crop information to receive a preliminary assessment. The platform communicates uncertainty and identifies missing information rather than presenting estimates as definitive laboratory results.
  • Climate Intelligence: The platform uses environmental information from NASA POWER and weather data services to help users explore climate conditions relevant to agricultural planning.
  • Crop Rotation Planning: Users can explore and compare different crop rotation strategies, considering their potential suitability, benefits, and risks.
  • Farm Economics: Users can enter estimated agricultural costs and expected returns to examine financial outcomes and compare possible plans.
  • Integrated Dashboard: The different tools are presented through a unified interface designed to make agricultural information easier to understand and navigate.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Agricultural decisions depend on interconnected factors, including soil conditions, climate variability, crop selection, and financial limitations. These factors are often considered separately.

VIRDARA aims to connect them in one accessible platform. Its intended impact is to support better-informed crop planning, encourage more thoughtful resource management, help users understand agricultural risks, and make environmental information more useful for practical decisions.

Technologies and Development Tools

VIRDARA was developed as a web application using:

  • React and TypeScript for the application structure and interactive functionality.
  • NASA POWER for accessible NASA-derived environmental and climate information.
  • Open-Meteo for weather information.
  • Bolt as an AI-assisted development environment.
  • Web-based data visualizations and interactive dashboard components to communicate information clearly.

Creativity and Innovation

VIRDARA's creative approach is its integration of environmental data and practical agricultural planning. Rather than presenting climate information, soil assessment, crop rotation, and economic calculations as separate tools, it brings them together to help users explore how these factors relate to one another.

The platform also emphasizes transparent information, understandable visualizations, and communicating uncertainty, which is particularly important when agricultural recommendations depend on incomplete or variable data.

Factors Considered

The project considers climate variability, soil information availability, crop rotation diversity, economic feasibility, agricultural risk, accessibility, and the importance of reliable data sources.

VIRDARA is designed to make complex environmental and agricultural information more understandable and useful, supporting a more informed approach to agricultural planning.
